investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T11:58–12:06Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod on the 6-node cluster: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity (0 allocatable slots remaining), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both node subsets. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) timed out without writing any evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-28 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new pods because 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent() to provision a remote VM-backed pod before it can poll state, the pod never becomes schedulable, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever written — causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state for ~126–143 seconds before the eval times out. Because pod scheduling is a prerequisite for agent creation, the eval runner never reaches the state-polling step, so no evidence payload is produced and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod on the 6-node cluster: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity (0 allocatable slots remaining), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both node subsets. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) timed out without writing any evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-28 because every pod created by the eval runner was stuck unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No agent was ever provisioned, so the runtime eval produced zero evidence and violated every field of its expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that are eligible to schedule peer-pod VMs. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never produced a running agent pod. Because no agent was created, the probe returned no evidence, causing a complete contract gap for all five required fields and failing the message assertion ("hello from aura"). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state all reporting 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata-capable nodes.
